extracted.intended_audience: public relations professionals and corporate/corporate-communications teams
extracted.subtask_description: A practitioner-focused rubric for modern press releases covering distribution effectiveness, quality standards (multimedia, methodology, spokespersons), crisis/ESG/DEI communications, and rising/declining tactics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multimedia inclusion required
rubrics_metrics.description: Multimedia inclusion now expected, not bonus; multimedia-first releases are rising.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed under 'State of the Industry', 'Quality Standards Industry-Wide', and 'What's Rising'. Treat multimedia as required rather than optional; avoid PDF-only attachments (declining).

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclose methodology for any data
rubrics_metrics.description: Methodology disclosure for any data is expected; demographic data should include methodology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appears under 'Quality Standards Industry-Wide' and in DEI guidance. Journalists are skeptical of unsourced claims, so include data methodology and sampling details when presenting statistics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spokesperson availability within 24 hours
rubrics_metrics.description: Spokesperson available within 24 hours for media inquiries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as an industry-wide quality standard and echoed in crisis guidance (named spokesperson with appropriate authority). Ensure someone is reachable within 24 hours.

rubrics_metrics.name: Named spokesperson with appropriate authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify a named spokesperson who has appropriate authority to speak on the issue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required especially in crisis communications; improves credibility and speeds journalist follow-ups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Named accountability owner
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify a named accountability owner for initiatives (especially DEI and ongoing programs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Included in DEI standards and the Quality Rubric. Naming an owner increases accountability and trust; avoid vague 'we are committed' statements without ownership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embargo lift times specified (PT/ET)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specify embargo lift times in PT/ET when using embargoes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Industry standard under 'Quality Standards Industry-Wide'. When offering embargoes, be explicit about time zone to avoid confusion for national outlets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translation availability for international news
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide translation availability for internationally relevant news.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed under 'Quality Standards Industry-Wide' — useful when targeting international audiences or global media.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledge crises within 2 hours
rubrics_metrics.description: Acknowledge the situation within 2 hours of news breaking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Crisis communication standard: rapid acknowledgement reduces rumor and shows responsiveness; follow with named spokesperson and factual updates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use specific facts, not statements of values (crisis)
rubrics_metrics.description: In crisis communications, emphasize specific facts rather than high-level value statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Crisis standard: journalists and audiences want concrete information (what happened, scope, next steps) rather than abstract apologies or value proclamations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide action steps, not just apology (crisis)
rubrics_metrics.description: Communicate concrete action steps in response to the incident, not solely apologies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Crisis guidance: include immediate remedial actions, timelines, and what affected parties can expect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specify update cadence for ongoing situations
rubrics_metrics.description: Define how often you will provide updates during an ongoing situation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Crisis protocol: set expectations for frequency of updates (e.g., hourly, daily) to maintain media trust and reduce speculation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use specific metrics for ESG communications
rubrics_metrics.description: ESG and sustainability communications should include specific metrics rather than vague commitments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under 'ESG and Sustainability Communications': quantify targets and performance to avoid vague claims and improve credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third-party verification for ESG claims
rubrics_metrics.description: When claiming ESG achievements, provide third-party verification where possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourages use of audits, certifications, or independent verification to substantiate sustainability claims and avoid skepticism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide timeline with milestones (ESG)
rubrics_metrics.description: Include timelines with milestones for ESG goals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ESG guidance: show credible, time-bound plans and interim milestones to demonstrate progress rather than open-ended promises.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledge unsolved challenges in ESG
rubrics_metrics.description: Be transparent about unresolved challenges when communicating ESG efforts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advises honesty about limitations to build trust and avoid accusations of greenwashing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid greenwashing language
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not use vague or exaggerated sustainability language that amounts to greenwashing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 'Avoid greenwashing language' is explicitly listed as an ESG standard; pair claims with metrics and verification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide demographic data with methodology (DEI)
rubrics_metrics.description: When making DEI claims, include demographic data and the methodology used to collect it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DEI standard: disclose sampling, definitions, and limits of the data to allow evaluation and reduce skepticism.

rubrics_metrics.name: DEI: specific actions, not aspirational language
rubrics_metrics.description: DEI communications should list specific actions rather than aspirational, high-level statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer concrete programs, timelines, and responsible parties over 'we aim to' phrasing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledge where DEI progress is needed
rubrics_metrics.description: Openly acknowledge areas where progress on DEI is lacking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transparency about shortcomings and plans to address them increases credibility; avoid performative statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid performative language (DEI)
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid performative or symbolic communications that lack substance or accountability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DEI standard: pair words with measurable actions and named accountability; don't rely on gestures without follow-through.

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct journalist outreach yields highest pickup
rubrics_metrics.description: Direct journalist outreach produces the highest pickup rates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under 'Distribution Channel Effectiveness': prioritize targeted outreach to reporters for story coverage; use wire services for SEO, not pickup.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wire services: lower pickup but high SEO
rubrics_metrics.description: Wire services tend to have the lowest media pickup but provide strong SEO benefits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use wires to boost discoverability and search visibility; supplement with direct outreach for actual pickups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Founder-led social media is rising in influence
rubrics_metrics.description: Social media activity led by founders is increasingly influential for distribution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leverage authentic founder voice and social channels to amplify releases and reach audiences directly.

rubrics_metrics.name: LinkedIn newsletters as emerging B2B channel
rubrics_metrics.description: LinkedIn newsletters are an emerging channel for B2B distribution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider LinkedIn newsletters for industry and professional audiences; it's a growing route to engaged readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Niche industry newsletters have high engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: Niche industry newsletters often deliver high engagement among target audiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Target vertical newsletters for specialist coverage and better engagement than broad channels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid generic 'leading provider' boilerplate
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid using generic 'leading provider' boilerplate language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed under 'What's Declining in Effectiveness' — boilerplate diminishes credibility and fails to differentiate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid quote-stuffed releases
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not overload releases with multiple or generic quotes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quote-stuffed releases are declining in effectiveness; use concise, meaningful quotes that add perspective or data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid PDF-only attachments
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not rely on PDF-only attachments for release distribution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PDF-only attachments reduce accessibility and multimedia capability; provide web-native assets and embedded media instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid Friday afternoon distribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid distributing news on Friday afternoons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as a declining tactic—Friday afternoon distribution often yields low pickup; time releases for higher-news windows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid embargoes without offering exclusivity
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not offer embargoes if you cannot provide an exclusivity benefit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 'Embargo without exclusivity' is declining—embargoes are less persuasive unless coupled with real journalist value (e.g., exclusives).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use original data reports
rubrics_metrics.description: Deploy original data reports as a content strategy to drive pickup and interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed under 'What's Rising' — original data differentiates content and supports media stories when accompanied by methodology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Founder-voice authenticity
rubrics_metrics.description: Emphasize authentic founder voice in communications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rising trend: founder-authored or founder-amplified releases perform well, especially on social platforms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-channel coordination
rubrics_metrics.description: Coordinate messaging across multiple channels (press, social, newsletters) for maximum impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlighted in 'What's Rising' and the Quality Rubric; plan release cadences and assets for each channel to reinforce coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include long-form context pieces alongside releases
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide long-form context pieces to accompany short releases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Long-form context helps reporters and readers understand background and significance; use when announcing complex data or initiatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personalization as a differentiator
rubrics_metrics.description: Personalization in outreach and messaging is becoming the key differentiator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under 'State of the Industry': tailor pitches and releases to specific outlets and reporters to improve pickup and engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be prepared for journalist skepticism of unsourced claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalists are increasingly skeptical of unsourced claims—provide sourcing, data, and verification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Called out in 'State of the Industry' — ensure claims are backed by data, methodology, or third-party verification to avoid being dismissed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific over aspirational
rubrics_metrics.description: Favor specific commitments, metrics, and actions over aspirational language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit in the Quality Rubric and reiterated across ESG/DEI and general guidance; specificity increases credibility and newsworthiness.
